newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-AJAX CLASH BECOMES MATCH OF HATE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-FEYENOORD-AJAX CLASH BECOMES MATCH OF HATE.

text.p: Feyenoord and Ajax have been rivals for nearly 100 years but that rivalry has now degenerated into a hate-fuelled ritual with violent fans hellbent on a level of destruction not witnessed since English hooliganism was at its height a decade ago.

"Feyenoord-Ajax has always been a classic," said newspaper Algemeen Dagblad on Monday, " but in the last few years, another tradition has developed: one of riots and violence. ... The duel between the two giants is now the Match of Hate."

While the players themselves provided a thrilling action-packed 133rd derby which ended in a 2-2 draw, the trouble surrounding the match turned the centre of Rotterdam into a virtual no-go area for several hours.
Police were highly visible on the streets, but they did not prevent a number of violent outbreaks.

Feyenoord fans lobbed a fire-bomb at police in the centre of the city and Ajax fans, arriving by train pelted police with ball bearings. Mounted police charged the supporters, making a number of arrests.
Near the stadium, Feyenoord fans attacked the Ajax team bus, throwing stones, bottles and sticks as well as a metal bar which broke one of the windows.

Ajax chairman Michael van Praag and a reserve player, Menno Willems were slightly injured in the ambush. According to newspaper De Telegraaf on Monday, the violence left the team prepared to call off the fixture, although, on television, coach Louis van Gaal said the hostilities had fired up his players for the start of the game.
In total some 30 troublemakers, mostly Feyenoord fans, were taken in by the police.
The trouble could have been worse. The kick-off was brought forward from from evening to early afternoon so that the police could control fans during daylight hours.
On balance, the police said they were satisfied with Sunday's operations.
"We assessed the situation fully and we believe it went reasonably well. Nothing more happened that would normally be the case for such a match," a police spokesman said.
Others were less content.

Feyenoord chairman Jorien van den Herik said he was pleased the game had been brought forward. Much worse could have happened with an evening kick-off. But on the whole, he said the violence left him unable to enjoy the game.
Opposition law and order spokesman Frans van den Heijden said he was "appalled" by the riots before the game and warned of worse to come.
"This cannot continue any longer. We are on the way to the first death unless we crack down," he said.
A member of the Dutch coalition government on Monday called for a debate on football vandalism, Dutch ANP news agency said.

The issue appeared at the top of the agenda after the Rotterdam violence, but debate was also stirred by a official report last week saying that football vandalism was not on the wane despite the efforts of the police.

The match itself, the first 2-2 draw between the two for 14 years, was marked by three penalties in the 15 minutes. The first, awarded after just twop minutes was blasted over the bar Ajax's Dutch international Patrick Kluivert, but two minutes Feyenoord's Ronald Koeman converted a penalty at the other end to put the home side ahead.

Ajax drew level after 15 minutes when Ronald de Boer scored from the spot but within a minute Bernard Schuiteman headed Feyenoord back iin front -- a lead they held until Kluivert equalised in the second half.

The play was heated, but the three penalty awards did not detract from a reasonably clean game. The result ended a run of five Ajax league victories in Rotterdam, but Kluivert's 71st minute strike -- Ajax's second equaliser of the game, spared the Amsterdam side the ultimate disgrace of losing to their Rotterdam rivals.
The ultimate winners on Sunday, however, were PSV Eindhoven whose 2-0 at AZ Alkmaar gave them a three-point cushion over second-placed Feyenoord. Ajax are fifth, 11 points adrift of the leaders.
